children: on Wednesday cut its 2027 revenue and earnings forecasts as delays to grid upgrades in Melbourne deferred the delivery and billing of contracted capacity at its M3 data centre.

The data centre operator now expects net revenue of A$475 million ($332.41 million) to A$500 million in 2027, down from its prior outlook of A$615 million to A$640 million, excluding the affected M3 contracts.
The company said delays to augmentation works by Jemena Electricity Networks meant the next increase in supply to its M3 Melbourne data centre is now expected in 2028.

NEXTDC said Jemena had suspended parts of the electricity network works needed to increase power supply to M3 due to opposition from the community and stakeholders and does not expect to recommence them before February 2027.

NEXTDC also said it now expects underlying earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of A$245 million to A$265 million in 2027, compared with its previous forecast of A$385 million to A$410 million, excluding the affected M3 contracts.
NEXTDC has three operational data centre projects in Melbourne, with two more currently under development.
Besides that, the firm has also built data centres across Sydney, Brisbane, Perth, Canberra, and Adelaide.

NEXTDC said it had put all new development projects and land acquisitions on hold for the foreseeable future and would evaluate capital recycling opportunities, including potential sales of selected development sites.

title: Australia's NEXTDC cuts 2027 earnings outlook after Melbourne data centre power delay
